report:
### Conclusion

Scientific evidence contradicts the view that the claim is false. Meta-analyses and clinical trials demonstrate that anti-cytokine drugs significantly reduce depressive symptoms in individuals with chronic inflammatory conditions.

### Key Findings

* **Efficacy in Clinical Trials:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of clinical trials in chronic inflammatory diseases (such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis, and inflammatory bowel disease) show that anti-cytokine therapies—including TNF-α and IL-6 inhibitors—significantly lower depressive symptoms (https://www.nature.com/articles/mp2016167).
* **Direct Neuropsychiatric Benefits:** Research investigating biologic therapies targeting inflammatory cytokines consistently shows clear neuropsychiatric improvements alongside physical disease management (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12428291/).
* **Independence from Physical Relief:** Analyses examining the relationship between physical healing (e.g., reduced joint pain or skin lesions) and mood improvement indicate that anti-cytokine medications exert an antidepressant effect independent of physical symptom reduction, supporting a direct link between peripheral inflammation and mood regulation (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5794896/).
* **Biological Mechanism:** Pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) contribute directly to neuroinflammation and treatment-resistant mood dysregulation, providing a clear biological rationale for targeting cytokine pathways to treat depressive symptoms (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0278584617308862).
